Enum Class MenuRegion

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<MenuRegion>
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.MenuRegion
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<MenuRegion>, Constable
public enum MenuRegion extends Enum<MenuRegion>
Named regions for positioning decoration panels inside vanilla menu screens. Each region anchors to the menu's container frame (leftPos/topPos/imageWidth/imageHeight) and declares a flow direction for stacking multiple panels in the same region.

Coverage. Eight edge regions — one for each of the four menu sides (left, right, top, bottom) combined with two alignment ends per side (top/bottom for vertical sides, left/right for horizontal sides). The SIDE_ALIGN_END naming reads as: "on SIDE of the menu, aligned to END, stacking away from END."

Plus three centered anchors — CENTER for centered-in-frame placement (Phase 14d-1 addition for modal dialogs), and TOP_CENTER / BOTTOM_CENTER for above-/below-the-frame placement centered on the horizontal axis (Phase 3b — Item 4a; brings MenuRegion to parity with HudRegion / ScreenRegion, which each carry TOP_CENTER / BOTTOM_CENTER / CENTER). CENTER is a single-position anchor; TOP_CENTER / BOTTOM_CENTER stack vertically away from the frame, each panel staying horizontally centered.

Flow direction — stacking grows away from the anchor end:

  • LEFT_ALIGN_TOP / RIGHT_ALIGN_TOP — flow down
  • LEFT_ALIGN_BOTTOM / RIGHT_ALIGN_BOTTOM — flow up
  • TOP_ALIGN_LEFT / BOTTOM_ALIGN_LEFT — flow right
  • TOP_ALIGN_RIGHT / BOTTOM_ALIGN_RIGHT — flow left
  • TOP_CENTER — flow up (above the frame, centered)
  • BOTTOM_CENTER — flow down (below the frame, centered)
  • CENTER — no stacking (single-position anchor)

See Design Docs/Phase 12/M5_REGION_SYSTEM.md for the full design and M5_REGION_SPECS.md for the authoritative region catalog.

    • TOP_CENTER

      public static final MenuRegion TOP_CENTER
      Above the menu's container frame, centered on the horizontal axis (Phase 3b — Item 4a). The panel renders at (leftPos + (imageWidth - panelWidth) / 2, topPos - panelHeight - STACK_GAP - prefix), so stacking grows UP (away from the menu), each sibling staying horizontally centered.

      Parity counterpart to HudRegion.TOP_CENTER / ScreenRegion.TOP_CENTER, anchored to the menu frame rather than the screen edge.

    • BOTTOM_CENTER

      public static final MenuRegion BOTTOM_CENTER
      Below the menu's container frame, centered on the horizontal axis (Phase 3b — Item 4a). The panel renders at (leftPos + (imageWidth - panelWidth) / 2, topPos + imageHeight + STACK_GAP + prefix), so stacking grows DOWN (away from the menu), each sibling staying horizontally centered.

      Parity counterpart to HudRegion.BOTTOM_CENTER / ScreenRegion.BOTTOM_CENTER.

    • CENTER

      public static final MenuRegion CENTER
      Centered within the menu's container frame. Canonical anchor for modal dialogs (Phase 14d-1). The panel renders at (leftPos + (imageWidth - panelWidth) / 2, topPos + (imageHeight - panelHeight) / 2).

      Stacking semantics: CENTER is a single-position anchor. Multiple panels registered with CENTER all resolve to the same origin and overlap (or, for modal dialogs, the consumer is expected to gate visibility so only one is up at a time).

      Centers within the menu's container frame, not the screen window. For most vanilla menus the frame is roughly mid-screen so the result looks visually centered; consumers wanting strict screen-window centering use a lambda-anchor adapter as the escape hatch.

    • isHorizontalFlow

      public boolean isHorizontalFlow()
      Returns true if panels in this region stack along the X axis.

      TOP_ALIGN / BOTTOM_ALIGN regions flow horizontally (panels arranged left-to-right or right-to-left above/below the menu frame). LEFT / RIGHT regions flow vertically. TOP_CENTER / BOTTOM_CENTER flow vertically (away from the frame, staying horizontally centered). CENTER does not stack — value is conventionally false.

    • priority

      public RegionAnchor<MenuRegion> priority(int priority)
      Returns a RegionAnchor pairing this region with an explicit stacking priority. Use when sibling panels in the same region need deterministic ordering relative to each other — pass the result anywhere a MenuRegion is accepted.

      Lower priority renders first (closer to the region's anchor edge). Default priority (when priority(int) is not called) is RegionAnchor.DEFAULT_PRIORITY (100); the registering mod's modId serves as the tiebreaker for siblings sharing a priority.
